question: Assess whether blood pressure changed significantly after treatment in 30 patients using a paired t-test. Report the mean difference, 95% confidence interval, and p-value.

files.eval_guideline: Mean difference and CI bounds must match the reference within 1% relative absolute error; p-value must match within +/-0.001; column order and header labels may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames are identical and both files are CSVs holding the paired t-test results.

parameters.question: Compare paired t-test results for blood pressure before/after treatment in 30 patients: mean difference and 95% CI bounds must match within 1% relative absolute error; p-value within +/-0.001; column order and header labels may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: A paired t-test always gives the same answer for the same data, and the output is a small results table (mean difference, CI, p-value). The guideline sets tolerances for each value and says column order and headers may differ, so approximate value-by-value matching fits.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables have one row with the summary of a single paired t-test, in the same layout, so no transpose is needed. All four reference columns have exact name matches in the candidate. The candidate's 11 extra columns (N, means, SD, t-statistic, etc.) are not used. Since there is only one row, rows are matched by position and no ID columns or sorting are needed. Permutation checking is pointless for a single row.

column_configs.name: Mean_Difference
column_configs.reasoning: This is the main result the task asks for, and the guideline sets a 1% RAE limit. The sign is kept because the reference reports After − Before.

column_configs.name: CI_95_Lower
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline sets a 1% RAE limit for the lower CI bound.

column_configs.name: CI_95_Upper
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline sets a 1% RAE limit for the upper CI bound.

column_configs.name: P_Value
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline allows an absolute error of ±0.001. Dividing 0.001 by the reference p-value (6.33e-12) gives a relative tolerance of about 1.58e8, so any candidate p-value within 0.001 of the reference counts as a match. This conversion uses the reference value in this table.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The task asks for three things: the mean difference, the 95% CI bounds and the p-value. Only the four reference columns are compared. The candidate's extra columns (Test, N, means, SD, SE, t, DF, Cohen's dz, significance flag, direction) are not in the reference, so they are left out. Column order and header labels are not checked. Mean_Difference, CI_95_Lower and CI_95_Upper use RAE with a tolerance of 0.01, which is the guideline's 1% rule. The guideline sets an absolute ±0.001 limit for the p-value, but RAE only measures relative error. To match the rule, the absolute limit is converted to a relative one using this table's single reference value: 0.001 / 6.33e-12 ≈ 1.58e8. The sign is kept for every column (compare_abs is false) because the reference uses After − Before. If a candidate used Before − After, the CI bounds would also swap places, so ignoring the sign would not make them match. With the candidate shown, all four values match the reference.
